anti_overlap: fd-finetuning-feasibility covers parameter updates from the pairs corpus
fd-reward-modeling-rlhf covers preference-based reward modeling and DPO
fd-constitutional-ai-refinement covers principle-based self-critique, not retrieval systems
fd-eval-benchmark-design covers measurement frameworks, not retrieval pipeline architecture
decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where retrieved examples introduce style or domain mismatch that degrades output — the wrong few-shot examples are worse than no examples.
focus: Few-shot RAG over the 8,250 editorial pairs as an inference-time approach and its tradeoffs vs parameter-efficient training
name: fd-retrieval-augmented-editing
persona: A retrieval systems engineer who has built dense retrieval pipelines for document-level tasks. Evaluates RAG designs against retrieval precision, prompt budget, and whether retrieved examples generalize or confuse the model.
review_areas: Review 2024-2026 literature on RAG for text editing: editorial retrieval (find the most stylistically similar source passage, inject its transformation as a few-shot example) vs principle retrieval
Evaluate embedding strategies for editorial pairs: sentence-BERT, Cohere Embed v3, or task-specific fine-tuned retrievers for before-text similarity vs style-cluster similarity
Assess prompt budget constraints: injecting 3-5 full before/after pairs into a multi-pass pipeline across 3 stages could consume 4,000-8,000 tokens per request
Review HyDE and other 2025 retrieval techniques for matching rough drafts to clean editorial analogues
Evaluate hybrid retrieval: sparse (BM25 on editorial principles + content keywords) + dense (embedding similarity)
Assess when RAG beats fine-tuning: for long-tail voice styles and niche domains, retrieved examples may generalize better than averaged training signal
success_hints: A RAG prototype should be benchmarkable against the existing prompt-only baseline using the LLM-as-judge rubrics already in place
Retrieval precision at k=5 must be measurable — without a retrieval eval the RAG recommendation is speculative
The 8,250-pair corpus is large enough for a dense retrieval index but the embedding model choice critically affects quality
task_context: Texturaize runs a multi-pass LLM editorial pipeline (developmental → line-edit → copy-edit) with a 19-principle editorial constitution derived via Inverse Constitutional AI from 1,000 professional pairs. The question is which training or inference-time approach beyond prompt engineering best leverages 8,250 curated pairs.
